title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
A Kansas couple, Matthew and Leah Spurlock, were stopped by police after their KU Alumni license plate, number 7007, matched a stolen temporary tag on a GMC pickup. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs and duplicates the same numbers across specialty plates, so automated Flock cameras flagged their minivan as stolen. Leah was pulled over in Colwich, Kansas, and about a month later Matthew was stopped in Catoosa, Oklahoma, where officers drew guns and handcuffed him before realizing the mistake.

Wichita police say Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds, and officers must confirm alerts, but if a stolen vehicle entry lists the wrong plate type, they have no choice but to stop the matching car. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit plate numbers to end duplicates, which police call the best fix. The Spurlocks' stolen tag entry has expired, so they are no longer worried and plan to keep their 14 year old plate.
